local-exception-file: lines 6-10 declare /etc/apparmor.d/local/usr.sbin.rsyslogd ensure file root:root 0644 and line 11 its content; probe stats owner/group/mode and cats the file, expect 'root root 644' then exactly '/srv/p8test-logs/ rw,' and '/srv/p8test-logs/** rwk,' as the fixture renders. On the clean node the file exists empty, so the content part makes the negative fail as it did.

profile-compiles-with-the-exception: line 16 reloads /etc/apparmor.d/usr.sbin.rsyslogd with apparmor_parser -r; probe preprocesses that same profile (apparmor_parser -p, includes resolved) and expects exactly the two logs_dir rules. It shows the on-disk profile carries the exception; that the LOADED profile carries it is shown by confined-rsyslogd-writes-to-logs-dir, since the stock profile does not grant /srv.

purpose covered: Purpose (header line 1: an AppArmor local exception so rsyslog can write to a custom log path; the manifest is one file + a refreshonly apparmor_parser -r notifying Service[rsyslog]) is read right and fully in the outcomes table. Checks test the exception file and its content/mode, the profile carrying it, rsyslogd still running confined in enforce mode after the reload chain, and the job itself: a confined rsyslogd actually writing a routed message into logs_dir (outside the stock /var/log grant), with a control that the same rsyslogd is still denied a syslog-owned directory outside the exception, so the profile rather than ownership decides. Nothing the lab can exercise is left out; no uncovered rows are needed (reboot-time profile loading is the apparmor service's, not this class's).
